surprises.description: BMRC reported diluted EPS of $0.62, above the preview’s $0.575 consensus estimate. That also reached the top of the preview’s $0.60–$0.62 inferred whisper range, rather than falling short of the higher buy-side bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net income rose to $9.9 million ($0.62 per share)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS ... $0.575”; the preview also put the “working whisper” at “$0.60–0.62.”

surprises.description: Margin expansion was stronger than the preview’s own estimate: the preview modeled a 6-basis-point sequential increase and cited a 3.44–3.45% June exit rate, while the call reported a 10-basis-point sequential expansion and a September tax-equivalent NIM of 3.54%. The September figure was about 3.46% excluding one-way deposit sales, so the exit-rate headline was stronger than the underlying comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin expanded 10 basis points sequentially”; “the September NIM was 3.54% tax-equivalent (about 3.46% excluding one-way deposit sales).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q3E NIM ... 3.44% (+6bp)”; the preview also identified “3.44–3.45%” as the June exit rate and said “Above 3.48% = re-rating.”

surprises.description: Deposits reversed the prior quarter’s outflow: deposits grew $25.3 million after falling $58.2 million in Q2, and noninterest-bearing deposits rose to 37.8% of the total from the preview’s cited 36.7%. That was better than the preview’s concern that deposit outflows might continue and its hope that they would merely stop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total deposits grew $25.3 million, including a $45 million increase in noninterest-bearing deposits, which now represent 37.8% of total deposits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Deposits fell $58M” in Q2; the preview said “Deposit outflows stop” in its bull scenario and warned that “deposits keep running off” in its bear scenario.

surprises.description: Management raised its estimate of the loan-yield benefit from repricing and remixing: the call cited roughly 25 basis points of monthly loan-yield benefit a year out, versus the preview’s cited estimate of about 20 basis points over the next 12 months. New fundings also came at a higher rate than the prior-quarter figure cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects roughly 25 basis points of monthly loan yield benefit a year out under a flat balance sheet, improved from about 20 basis points estimated last quarter”; new fundings were originated at “6.65% (up 12 bps).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “~20bp of loan-yield benefit over the next 12 months (~5bp/quarter)” and cited Q2 commitments at a “6.53% weighted-average rate.”

surprises.description: Payoffs fell sharply, which the call attributed in part to resolving problematic pandemic-era CRE and wine loans and described as a normalizing trend. The preview focused on pipeline conversion and the risk of continued balance-sheet shrinkage but did not anticipate this payoff decline or the resolution of those loans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payoffs fell sharply to $31.6 million from $71 million, including resolution of about $28 million of problematic pandemic-era CRE and wine industry loans, signaling a normalizing payoff trend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 was when the loan pipeline “should convert” and warned that if it did not, “the growth story slips to 2027”; it gave no payoff estimate.

surprises.description: Credit was not entirely free of migration: a $114 million owner-occupied CRE relationship was downgraded, contrary to the preview’s baseline of no new migration. The borrower was paying as agreed with no expected loss, but loan and unfunded-commitment provisions totaled $825,000, above the preview’s roughly $300,000 assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $114 million owner-occupied CRE relationship was downgraded due to a borrower-specific issue, but the borrower is paying as agreed with no expected loss”; there was “a $500,000 loan provision and $325,000 unfunded commitment provision.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the credit bar was “simply ‘no new migration’” and modeled a “+$0.3M” provision, with consensus at “~+$0.3M.”

surprises.description: Rising rates drove a marked deterioration in tangible capital and book value, instead of the improvement the preview expected: TCE fell to 8.05% from 8.52%, and tangible book value was $18.81 rather than the preview’s expected increase from $19.92. CET1 improved to 12.96%, but that did not offset the AOCI-driven decline in the tangible measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rising market rates reduced AOCI by $24.8 million, lowering the tangible common equity ratio to 8.05% and tangible book value to $18.81, while CET1 improved to 12.96%.”
